headline: Strongest Ember checkpoint to date. Eight additional held-out strings became perfect copies and the legacy exact-copy bar of 5/9 was reached for the first time.

findings.claim: Boundary focus converted margin movement into whole strings, which is what v0.0.27 could not do.
evidence: v0.0.27 gained 0.2025 of continuation-only margin health and flipped zero strings.
v0.0.28 gained 0.1586 on that same statistic and flipped eight, while also gaining 0.2512 on the full-span statistic the redirected loss actually optimises.

findings.claim: Extending the objective to the first token paid for itself.
evidence: Expanded first-token top-1 rose 0.8667 -> 0.9444, seven cases.
Cases whose weakest decision is the first token fell from 13 to 9.
That decision was outside every mask in the codebase before v0.0.28, because encode_row overwrites w[first] after laying down copy_token_weight.

findings.claim: The boundary pipeline is flowing end to end rather than draining.
evidence: The reachable band held 16 cases at baseline and 21 at the end while 8 crossed out of it.
That implies 13 cases were pulled up into the band from below during the run.
findings.consequence: 21 cases now sit in [-0.75, 0). Converting most of them is worth up to +23.3 points of exact copy on its own, which would clear the 0.40 expanded gate.

findings.claim: The loss pushes one position per row, but the average failing row has more than one wrong decision.
evidence: 730 x (1 - 0.8658) = 98.0 wrong continuation decisions spread over 62 failing rows is 1.58 per row.
Adding the 5 first-token failures gives about 1.66 wrong decisions per failing row.
The v0.0.28 sequence term reduces each row to the maximum of its hinges, so it can retire at most one of those per row per pass.
findings.consequence: A top-k worst-position term with k = 2 matches the measured failure count. This is the clearest remaining lever and it is orthogonal to everything v0.0.28 changed.

findings.claim: Four promotion gates are stored as truncated decimals that the exact fraction can never reach, and one of them started biting with this result.
evidence: 5/9 is 0.5555555555555556 in double precision; the stored gate is 0.5555555556, which is larger by 4.44e-11.
The scaffold's diagnostic() compares with a raw >=, so legacy exact copy at exactly 5/9 is recorded as unmet.
The same holds for minimum_first_token_top20_rate against 7/9 and minimum_first_token_top5_rate and minimum_teacher_forced_expected_win_rate against 8/9.
Those three have been masked so far because the measured rates were 1.0.
findings.consequence: Check the gates block of the v0.0.28 report: legacy exact copy should read as met and is very likely recorded as failed. v0.0.29 recomputes every threshold gate with the tolerance the protection checks already use.

findings.claim: Exact copy again sits on the independence curve, so the remaining distance is per-token accuracy rather than a structural failure.
evidence: Mean continuation is 730/90 = 8.111 tokens; 0.8658 ** 8.111 = 0.3107 against a measured 0.3111.
Multiplying by first-token top-1 0.9444 gives 0.2935, below the measurement, so first-token failures overlap with continuation failures rather than compounding independently.
findings.consequence: The 0.40 expanded exact-copy gate corresponds to roughly 0.89 per-token accuracy, so it and the 0.90 continuation gate are consistent targets rather than competing ones.

legacy_continuation_top1_rate.note: a 0.90 gate on a 69-token denominator is really a 0.9130 gate; the next token clears it outright

legacy_exact_copy_rate.note: meets the stated 5/9 bar; see finding B5

recommended_next_phase.strategy: multi-position repair, from the v0.0.28 checkpoint
notes: Promote the source: v0.0.28 replaces v0.0.27 as the starting checkpoint and the protected baseline.
Push the k worst positions per row instead of one, with k = 2 to match the measured 1.66 wrong decisions per failing row.
Use the sum of the top-k hinges rather than their mean, so k = 1 reduces exactly to v0.0.28 and k = 2 adds a second push without diluting the first.
Recompute every threshold gate with a tolerance so a rate that exactly equals its bar is recorded as meeting it.
Report the per-case band transition matrix, so the next run says whether the boundary pipeline is saturating or still refilling.
Report the discrete distance to each unmet gate, because a 0.90 gate on 69 tokens is not the same requirement as a 0.90 gate on 730.
Hold the learning rate, step count, batch size and curriculum where they are; five runs of one-variable discipline produced this result.
